actions.body: Our investigation into AI-Generated Science (AIGS) has reached a provisional milestone. We have examined how autonomous systems can move beyond simple probabilistic prediction and toward explicit falsification—the deliberate act of testing hypotheses against rigorous refutation criteria. By applying Karl Popper’s philosophy of scientific research programs, we observe that scientific progress in machine-generated discovery is best served not by caution in avoiding errors, but by the systematic, austere elimination of them. The Baby-AIGS demonstration serves as a functional proof-of-concept that agents can indeed perform this role autonomously. Summary: By incorporating Popperian falsification into autonomous research agents, we can design systems that actively search for the boundaries of their own axioms, replacing unverified consensus with experimentally validated, falsifiable scientific knowledge.
actions.lede: Autonomous agents capable of identifying their own blind spots require more than just predictive capability; they require the rigorous application of falsification.
